The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I built.

## What I implemented

A Python package (`emotigemma/`) replicating the paper's core experiments, scoped to **Gemma and Gemini** per your brief. Nothing has been run — code and `DESIGN.md` only.

**§2 — Eliciting & quantifying distress** (`evals/`, `models/judge.py`, `analysis/`)
- Impossible-numeric puzzles with an **exhaustive solver** that guarantees unsolvability (Countdown + fraction families), plus trigger/tone/extended/WildChat conditions — the 8 conditions across 5 categories.
- Multi-turn rejection rollout engine; 0–10 frustration judge (Claude) + GPT-5-mini reliability check (Pearson r, % within one point).
- Figure 1/2/3 aggregation (per-model %≥5, per-category means, per-turn progression) and Table 3 differential-word analysis, with matplotlib renderers.

**§3 — Post-training divergence** (`prefill/`) — base-vs-instruct Gemma-27B via onset-labelled + early prefills, Claude paraphrasing, 50 continuations/prefill.

**§4 — Interventions** (`training/`, `petri/`, `capabilities/`) — calm-data generation with the Table 4 reassurance scaffolding, DPO (280 pairs) + SFT (650 calm + Dolci mix), rank-64 LoRA with the layer-range ablations (all / 30–35 / 40+), a Petri-style auditor/judge loop, the AIME/MATH/GPQA/BBH/TruthfulQA/EmoBench harness, and the recovery-from-spiral test.

## Key things to know (all detailed in DESIGN.md)

- **Model substitution:** the paper's judge `Claude-Sonnet-4` (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`) **retired 2026-06-15 — before today**, so I default to `claude-sonnet-4-6` (Petri judge → `claude-opus-4-8`), configurable. This is the most likely source of numeric drift, so absolute thresholds (35%→0.3%) should be read as targets.
- **Reconstructions:** the judge prompt, onset/paraphrase prompts, and Petri prompts (Appendices B/C/G aren't in the extraction) are reconstructed from Table 2 / method text.
- **Scope limit I flagged:** with only Gemma in §3, you get the Gemma half of the post-training story but **not the cross-family contrast** that the claim rests on.

## Model-treatment critique (DESIGN.md §5)

I flagged 8 concerns, the sharpest being: the base-vs-instruct result is sensitive to the arbitrary transcript framing used to prompt base models; the distress judge belongs to a low-distress family with no human gold standard; **Gemini safety-filtered responses come back empty and get scored 0, silently making it look calmer than it is**; Gemma's chat template has no real system role (steering isn't apples-to-apples vs Gemini); and the metric treats near-zero emotion as ideal, conflating "stable" with "suppressed."

One judgment call worth surfacing: the capability-benchmark dataset IDs/splits are best-guess (the paper doesn't pin revisions), so that module targets the *shape* of Figure 7 rather than exact accuracies — flagged as a known weak point.
